note: The session's shared web search budget ran out after ten searches for this part, so most of it was done by fetching official county pages and the Montana Free Press 2026 legislative guide (projects.montanafreepress.org/election-guide-2026/legislative-candidates-by-district/, a named news organization), which lists campaign websites; every website below was then opened and checked to name the candidate and the office or district. Some addresses were found by trying likely names (jeffersonforhd26.com, willisformontana.com). Left out on purpose: calebhinkle.com is Caleb Hinkle's 2024 House District 68 site, not his 2026 Senate District 34 race; michaelsaul.com is a production company and not tied to the House District 72 candidate; Carl Marquardt appears in the Sanders County staff directory as a Justice Court clerk, which is employment, not an office; Michelle Bianco's site says she served on a library board without naming the body or years; the Gallatin County history of elected officials page does not list Roger Blank, so he is not shown as holding the office (Eric Semerad holds it). flathead.mt.gov did not resolve, so Brad Abell's office comes from the Flathead Beacon. Party pages already in ballot/lean/mt_endorsements.json under other_support (slate cards, honor roll, the Cascade and Lewis and Clark Democrats' lists) are not endorsements and are not repeated here. Sitting legislators (state_member_id) were given websites, endorsements and own words only.
